title: The Italian Renaissance
description: Harmony, perspective, and humanism from the rebirth of classical ideals.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: Virgin and Child with an Angel
items.description_narrative: Sandro Botticelli's 'Virgin and Child with an Angel' is a delicate tempera on panel painting created between 1475 and 1485. It depicts a tender moment between the Virgin Mary, the Christ Child, and a watchful angel.
items.tags: religious art, renaissance, italian, madonna, sacred, serene, tempera painting

items.title: Virgin and Child with Two Angels
items.description_narrative: Sandro Botticelli's "Virgin and Child with Two Angels" depicts Mary tenderly holding the infant Christ, accompanied by two celestial figures. This tempera on panel artwork showcases the delicate forms and devotional sentiment characteristic of the artist's Florentine Renaissance style.
items.tags: religious art, renaissance, virgin and child, tempera, florentine, devotional, serene, italian art

items.title: Allegory of Venus and Cupid
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas, titled "Allegory of Venus and Cupid," depicts classical mythological figures associated with love and desire. Created around 1600 by an imitator of Titian, it reflects themes popular in Renaissance Venetian art.
items.tags: mythology, allegory, classical, renaissance, venetian, love, oil painting, human figures

items.title: Portrait of a Lady
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas depicts a dignified lady, rendered with the rich colors and subtle modeling characteristic of Venetian Renaissance portraiture. Created around 1550, it reflects the artistic style of Titian's workshop or a close follower.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, renaissance, lady, venetian art, sixteenth century

items.title: Scenes from the Life of Saint John the Baptist
items.description_narrative: This tempera on panel artwork, 'Scenes from the Life of Saint John the Baptist,' was created by Bartolomeo di Giovanni. Dating from around 1490–95, it vividly depicts significant moments from the saint's life.
items.tags: religious, narrative, early renaissance, italian, tempera, saint john the baptist

items.title: The Nativity
items.description_narrative: Fra Bartolommeo's 'The Nativity' depicts the birth of Jesus Christ, a central event in Christian theology. This oil on panel painting showcases the artist's High Renaissance style and devotion.
items.tags: nativity, religious art, christianity, renaissance, high renaissance, italian art, sacred, oil painting

items.title: Alessandro de' Medici
items.description_narrative: Pontormo's oil on panel portrait captures Alessandro de' Medici, Duke of Florence, with a penetrating gaze, reflecting his powerful status. This work exemplifies the distinctive Mannerist style prevalent in the mid-16th century Italian Renaissance.
items.tags: portrait, mannerism, italian renaissance, medici, nobility, oil painting, 16th century

items.title: Christ Carrying the Cross
items.description_narrative: Sebastiano del Piombo captures the dramatic moment of Christ carrying the cross towards his crucifixion, a powerful depiction of suffering and resolve. This oil on panel painting by Sebastiano del Piombo vividly portrays Christ's arduous journey, highlighting the profound emotional weight of the event.
items.tags: christ, crucifixion, religious art, high renaissance, italian, suffering, dramatic, oil painting

items.title: The Crucifixion
items.description_narrative: Carlo Crivelli's 'The Crucifixion', painted around 1487, depicts the central Christian narrative with his characteristic tempera on panel technique. This work exemplifies his meticulous detail and expressive figural style, typical of the late 15th century.
items.tags: religious, renaissance, tempera, italian, biblical, narrative, devotional, early renaissance

items.title: Saint John the Baptist Entering the Wilderness
items.description_narrative: Giovanni di Paolo depicts Saint John the Baptist embarking on his spiritual journey into the wilderness in this tempera on panel painting. The artwork showcases the artist's distinctive style, characterized by its vibrant color and intricate narrative detail.
items.tags: religious, early renaissance, sienese school, tempera, narrative, spiritual, wilderness

items.title: Ecce Agnus Dei
items.description_narrative: Giovanni di Paolo's 'Ecce Agnus Dei' depicts John the Baptist gesturing towards Jesus Christ, emphasizing Christ's role as the Lamb of God. This tempera on panel painting exemplifies the distinct narrative and spiritual intensity of Sienese art.
items.tags: religious, biblical, sienese, quattrocento, tempera, italian, devotional, early renaissance

items.title: The Assassination and Funeral of Julius Caesar
items.medium: Tempera on panel, transferred to canvas mounted on pressed hardboard and cradled
items.description_narrative: This painting vividly depicts the dramatic assassination and subsequent funeral of Julius Caesar, a pivotal event in Roman history. Created by the Workshop of Apollonio di Giovanni, this tempera on panel artwork captures the narrative intensity of these historical moments.
items.tags: roman history, julius caesar, assassination, funeral, renaissance, italian art, narrative, historical

items.title: The Adventures of Ulysses
items.description_narrative: This tempera on panel painting illustrates scenes from Homer's Odyssey, chronicling the epic journey of the hero Ulysses. Created during the early 15th century, it brings to life tales of ancient mythology.
items.tags: mythology, epic, ancient greece, early renaissance, narrative, italian, tempera

items.title: The Last Communion of Saint Jerome
items.description_narrative: Botticelli's 'The Last Communion of Saint Jerome' depicts the aged saint receiving his final communion before death, a poignant moment of devotion. Rendered in tempera and gold on wood, this painting exemplifies the meticulous craftsmanship characteristic of its era.
items.tags: religious, devotional, christian, saint jerome, renaissance, italian, tempera

items.title: The Annunciation
items.description_narrative: Botticelli's 'The Annunciation' depicts the pivotal biblical moment when the Archangel Gabriel announces to Mary that she will conceive the Son of God. Rendered with tempera and gold on wood, this work exemplifies the luminous artistry of the Early Renaissance.
items.tags: annunciation, religious, christian art, renaissance, italian, tempera, devotional

items.title: Mona Lisa
items.description_narrative: The most famous painting in the world. It depicts Lisa Gherardini, wife of Francesco del Giocondo, sitting in front of an imaginary landscape. Her enigmatic expression and the masterful use of sfumato make it a masterpiece of the Renaissance.
items.tags: portrait, renaissance, sfumato, enigmatic, female

items.title: The Birth of Venus
items.description_narrative: The goddess Venus emerges from the sea as a fully grown woman, arriving at the shore on a giant scallop shell. One of the world's most famous and appreciated works of art, it has become a landmark of Italian Renaissance painting.
items.tags: mythology, venus, renaissance, goddess, shell, classical

items.title: The Creation of Adam
items.description_narrative: The most famous section of the Sistine Chapel ceiling. God reaches out to give life to Adam, their fingers nearly touching. This single gesture has become one of the most replicated religious images and an enduring icon of humanity.
items.tags: fresco, sistine chapel, genesis, god, adam, renaissance

items.title: The School of Athens
items.description_narrative: A fresco in the Apostolic Palace in the Vatican depicting a congregation of the greatest philosophers, mathematicians, and scientists of antiquity, with Plato and Aristotle at the center. It is considered a masterpiece of perspective and one of the greatest achievements of Renaissance art.
items.tags: philosophy, plato, aristotle, fresco, renaissance, architecture

items.title: The Last Supper
items.description_narrative: Painted on the refectory wall of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, Leonardo captures the instant Christ announces that one of the Twelve Apostles will betray him, freezing each figure mid-reaction. Its rigorous perspective and psychological drama made it one of the most studied and reproduced compositions in Western art.
items.tags: renaissance, religious, fresco, italian, dramatic, iconic, milan

items.title: Primavera
items.description_narrative: A procession of mythological figures - Venus, the Three Graces, Flora, and Mercury - drifts through an orange grove in one of the most celebrated allegories of the Florentine Renaissance. Botticelli's linear grace and flowering meadow have made it an emblem of Renaissance humanism.
items.tags: renaissance, mythology, allegory, florentine, springtime, elegant, botticelli

items.title: Venus of Urbino
items.description_narrative: A reclining nude gazes directly at the viewer from a sumptuous Venetian interior, her pose derived from Giorgione but charged with new immediacy and warmth. The painting became the touchstone for centuries of reclining-nude compositions, from Manet's Olympia onward.
items.tags: renaissance, venetian, nude, sensual, domestic, titian, masterpiece

items.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
items.description_narrative: Bacchus leaps from his chariot toward the abandoned Ariadne in a whirl of leopards, satyrs, and brilliant ultramarine sky. Painted for the Duke of Ferrara's private study, it remains one of the most vividly colored mythological scenes of the Italian Renaissance.
items.tags: renaissance, mythology, venetian, dynamic, colorful, titian, movement

items.title: The Wedding at Cana
items.description_narrative: Christ's first miracle, turning water into wine, unfolds amid a vast banquet of over a hundred contemporary Venetian figures, musicians, and architecture. At nearly ten meters wide, it stands among the largest and most theatrically staged paintings of the Renaissance.
items.tags: renaissance, religious, venetian, banquet, monumental, crowded, veronese

items.title: The Last Judgment
items.description_narrative: Covering the altar wall of the Sistine Chapel, Christ presides over the resurrection of the dead, the saved ascending and the damned cast down in a swirling mass of muscular bodies. Its sculptural intensity and unflinching nudity provoked controversy even as it cemented Michelangelo's reputation as the supreme master of the human form.
items.tags: renaissance, religious, fresco, sistine chapel, dramatic, monumental, michelangelo

items.title: Virgin of the Rocks
items.medium: Oil on panel, transferred to canvas
items.description_narrative: The Louvre's version of Leonardo's altarpiece, one of two nearly identical compositions he painted, showing the Virgin, the infant Christ, the young John the Baptist, and an angel in a shadowy grotto. It is a defining demonstration of Leonardo's sfumato technique, with figures modeled in soft gradations of light and shade rather than hard outlines.

items.title: The Sistine Madonna
items.description_narrative: Commissioned by Pope Julius II as an altarpiece for the church of San Sisto in Piacenza, the painting shows the Madonna descending through parted curtains with the Christ Child, flanked by Saint Sixtus and Saint Barbara. The two winged putti daydreaming at the base of the composition became independently famous, endlessly reproduced on their own.

items.title: Pallas and the Centaur
items.description_narrative: The armed figure of Pallas Athena restrains a centaur by the hair, widely read as an allegory of reason subduing base instinct. Her gown is patterned with the interlaced diamond-ring emblem of the Medici, tying the work to the family's patronage.

items.title: The Battle of San Romano
items.medium: Egg tempera with oil on poplar panel
items.description_narrative: The National Gallery's panel, one of three depicting the 1432 battle between Florence and Siena, shows Florentine commander Niccolo da Tolentino leading the cavalry charge. Broken lances and fallen soldiers are arranged along calculated orthogonal lines, an early showcase of Renaissance linear perspective.

items.title: The Lamentation over the Dead Christ
items.description_narrative: Mantegna presents the body of the dead Christ in extreme foreshortening, drawing the viewer almost to the soles of his feet in a radical compositional experiment. The Virgin Mary, Saint John, and Mary Magdalene mourn at the edge of the marble slab in a stark, emotionally intense scene.

items.title: Virgin and Child with the Young Saint John the Baptist
items.description_narrative: Painted early in Correggio's career, this intimate panel shows the soft modeling and gentle sentiment that would define his mature style as a leading painter of the Parma school. The composition places the infant Christ and the young Saint John the Baptist in tender interaction with the Virgin.

items.title: Tarquin and Lucretia
items.description_narrative: Tintoretto depicted the ancient Roman legend of Tarquin's assault on Lucretia with the dramatic diagonal composition and dynamic movement characteristic of Venetian Mannerism. The subject was popular among Renaissance patrons as an exemplar of virtue and honor.

items.title: Annunciation
items.description_narrative: Fra Angelico masterfully depicts the pivotal moment of the Annunciation, where the Archangel Gabriel conveys the divine message to the Virgin Mary. The scene is imbued with serene beauty and spiritual grace, characterized by the artist's use of radiant colors and delicate forms.
items.tags: early renaissance, christian art, religious, annunciation, mary, gabriel, italian, spiritual

items.title: Ghent Altarpiece: Adoration of the Mystic Lamb
items.description_narrative: Jan van Eyck's iconic Ghent Altarpiece, specifically the 'Adoration of the Mystic Lamb' panel, is a pivotal work in art history. This complex, multi-paneled artwork is renowned for its meticulous detail, vibrant colors, and profound theological narrative.
items.tags: religious art, altarpiece, early netherlandish, christianity, northern renaissance, adoration, sacred, detailed

items.title: The Annunciation
items.description_narrative: Petrus Christus's 'The Annunciation' depicts the pivotal biblical moment when the Archangel Gabriel announces to Mary that she will conceive Jesus. This significant oil on wood panel exemplifies the detailed artistry of early Netherlandish painting.
items.tags: annunciation, biblical, religious, oil painting, early netherlandish, sacred, petrus christus

items.title: Portrait of a Young Man
items.description_narrative: Bronzino's 'Portrait of a Young Man,' painted in oil on wood during the 1530s, exemplifies the artist's refined style and meticulous detail. The sitter's composed expression and elegant demeanor reflect the sophisticated portraiture characteristic of the period.
items.tags: portrait, young man, mannerism, italian renaissance, elegant, intense, sophisticated

items.title: Jacob Willemsz van Veen (1456–1535), the Artist's Father
items.description_narrative: Maarten van Heemskerck captures his father, Jacob Willemsz van Veen, in this striking portrait. Executed in oil on wood in 1532, the work offers a personal glimpse into the artist's family.
items.tags: portrait, old master, oil painting, father, renaissance, 16th century, dutch art

items.title: Hermann von Wedigh III (died 1560)
items.description_narrative: Hans Holbein the Younger masterfully depicted Hermann von Wedigh III in this striking oil and gold on oak portrait. Painted in 1532, this work exemplifies Holbein's meticulous realism and attention to detail.
items.tags: portrait, renaissance, northern renaissance, 16th century, german, oil painting, formal, realism

items.title: Portrait of Alvise Contarini(?); (verso) A Tethered Roebuck
items.medium: Oil on wood; verso: oil and gold on wood
items.description_narrative: This painting features a probable portrait of Alvise Contarini on the front, rendered in oil on wood. The reverse side reveals 'A Tethered Roebuck,' executed with oil and gold on wood, showcasing the dual nature of the artwork.
items.tags: portrait, renaissance, italian, oil painting, roebuck, contemplative, venetian, 15th century

items.title: Tommaso di Folco Portinari (1428–1501); Maria Portinari (Maria Maddalena Baroncelli, born 1456)
items.description_narrative: These oil portraits depict Tommaso di Folco Portinari and Maria Maddalena Baroncelli, meticulously rendered by Hans Memling. Created around 1470, these works exemplify the detailed portraiture of the period.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, Northern Renaissance, 15th century, realism, Flemish art
